title: Disney Nerd Nightmare
intro: [whispers] Welcome to the Disney Nerd Nightmare. [laughs] Every clue on this board is a deep cut, from the animation desk to the tunnels under the parks. If you get a two-hundred wrong today, nobody will judge you. [chuckles] Okay, we'll judge you a little.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A dim, cluttered archive room after midnight, stacks of old animation cels, film canisters, blueprints of a castle, a glowing desk lamp and dust floating in the light.

categories.title: Ink and Paint Department
categories.intro: We open in the animation building. Ink and Paint Department is about how the movies were actually made.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. An old animation studio desk with a backlit animation disk, pencil sketches, jars of paint and clear acetate cels drying on a rack.

clues.clue: Pixar's Toy Story, the first feature film made entirely with computer animation, came out in this year.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 1995! [excited] Released in November, and animation was never the same again.

clues.clue: Walt Disney voiced Mickey Mouse until 1947, when this Disney sound-effects man took over the role.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Jimmy MacDonald! He voiced Mickey for about thirty years, then passed the ears to Wayne Allwine.

clues.clue: This Nine Old Men animator, who designed Jiminy Cricket, played trombone in the Disney jazz band Firehouse Five Plus Two.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Ward Kimball! [laughs] Animator, trombonist and train fan. A locomotive at Disneyland is named after him.

clues.clue: This 1961 film was the first Disney feature to use the Xerox process, copying drawings straight onto cels.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is One Hundred and One Dalmatians! Xerox made drawing all those spots possible, and gave the film its sketchy look.

clues.clue: Disney's digital CAPS system was first used to ink and paint an entire feature on this 1990 film.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is The Rescuers Down Under! [gasps] It was the first feature finished fully digitally. The Little Mermaid used CAPS for just its final rainbow scene.

categories.title: Classified Disney
categories.intro: [whispers] Shh. This category is about the hidden spots the parks don't put on the map.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A secret door in a quaint old-town street at night, a single lamp glowing in an upstairs window, a keyhole glinting.

clues.clue: This members-only club in Disneyland's New Orleans Square is named for its street address.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Club 33! [whispers] Look for a small door with a number plate. And bring a very big wallet.

clues.clue: Walt Disney had a private apartment above this Main Street building at Disneyland, and a lamp still burns in its window.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Fire Station! The lamp in the window is kept lit to honor Walt.

clues.clue: Walt planned a second private apartment above this New Orleans Square attraction. It later became the Disneyland Dream Suite.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Pirates of the Caribbean! [sighs] Walt never got to live there. Today it's a very fancy suite above the pirates.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom's network of service tunnels has a nickname that joins utility and corridors.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Utilidors! [chuckles] They're actually at ground level. The park was built on top of them, like a second floor.

clues.clue: Climbers in Disneyland's Matterhorn can take a break with this piece of sports gear hidden inside the mountain.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a basketball hoop! [laughs] A small half court, way up inside the mountain. Nothing but net.

categories.title: Extinct Attractions Zoom
categories.intro: [gasps] Zoom time! We're zooming in on artwork of attractions that are long gone. Name the ride.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A foggy graveyard of retired theme park ride vehicles, a vintage motorcar, a submarine hull and a futuristic pod, lit by soft moonlight.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom closed its version of this wild motorcar ride in 1998. It still drives at Disneyland.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mr. Toad's Wild Ride! [laughs] A ride that ends with you in, well, a very warm place. Classic.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. Extreme close-up of a green vintage open-top motorcar crashing through a painted English country manor, papers flying, crooked signposts, wild colourful set pieces.

clues.clue: This EPCOT dark ride from 1983 to 1999 showed off future homes in the desert, under the sea and in space.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Horizons! [sighs] Riders got to pick their own ending. Fans still miss it.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. Extreme close-up of a glowing orange-lit space colony window looking out at a planet, a desert farm with hydroponic oranges below, and a city under the sea.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom's lagoon was home to this submarine ride until 1994.
clues.answer: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea: Submarine Voyage
accept: 20,000 leagues under the sea: submarine voyage
twenty thousand leagues under the sea
choices: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea: Submarine Voyage
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea! The subs didn't actually dive. They just sank a little and slid along a track.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. Extreme close-up of a riveted grey-green Victorian-style submarine with a jagged dorsal fin and round portholes, gliding through a turquoise lagoon past fake coral and a sea serpent.

clues.clue: From 1967 to 1985, this Disneyland ride let guests shrink small enough to fly into a snowflake.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Adventure Thru Inner Space! [gasps] Blue pod vehicles called Atomobiles went through a giant microscope. Star Tours took its spot.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. Extreme close-up of a giant silver laboratory microscope with blue capsule-shaped ride vehicles disappearing into its lens, swirling giant snowflake crystals and glowing molecules.

clues.clue: This EPCOT simulator, open from 1989 to 2007, sent guests into a human bloodstream.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Body Wars! [laughs] A shrinking mission inside the human body. Also known as the bumpiest ride at EPCOT.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. Extreme close-up of a sleek miniature vehicle racing through a red tunnel of giant floating blood cells, glowing white cells and pulsing arteries.

categories.title: Off the Deep End
categories.intro: Parks people, this one is for you. Off the Deep End is all heights, dates and a little railroad history.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. Detailed architectural blueprints of a fairy-tale castle and an old steam locomotive spread across a drafting table with rulers and a compass.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom's Cinderella Castle stands this many feet tall.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 189 feet! Tricks of forced perspective make it look even taller.

clues.clue: Disneyland's smaller Sleeping Beauty Castle rises about this many feet.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 77 feet! [chuckles] Walt wanted a friendly castle, not a scary fortress.

clues.clue: The Hollywood Tower Hotel at Disney's Hollywood Studios is this tall, just short of needing aircraft warning lights.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 199 feet! [laughs] One more foot and it would need blinking red warning lights on top.

clues.clue: Tokyo Disneyland, the first Disney park outside the United States, opened in this year.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 1983! It opened on April 15th, just a few months after EPCOT Center.

clues.clue: Disneyland Railroad engine number one is named for this Santa Fe Railway founder.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the C. K. Holliday! [excited] Named for Cyrus K. Holliday. The Santa Fe Railway sponsored the railroad when the park opened.

categories.title: Voices from the Vault
categories.intro: Our wildcard is all about the voice actors. Name the voices behind the characters.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A vintage radio studio with a big ribbon microphone on a stand, script pages on a music stand and a glowing ON AIR lamp with no lettering.

clues.clue: This man was the original voice of Donald Duck, for about fifty years.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Clarence Nash! [laughs] Nickname: Ducky. Of course.

clues.clue: Goofy's first voice, and his famous holler, came from this performer.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Pinto Colvig! He also voiced the dwarfs Grumpy and Sleepy. Gawrsh!

clues.clue: He voiced Winnie the Pooh, Kaa the snake and the Cheshire Cat.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Sterling Holloway! [chuckles] He was also the stork in Dumbo. What a voice.

clues.clue: His deep bass sings Grim Grinning Ghosts in the Haunted Mansion, and he gave Tony the Tiger his roar.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Thurl Ravenscroft! [laughs] He's the singing bust with the broken nose. Grrreat!

clues.clue: This voice actor is the Ghost Host of the Haunted Mansion and also voiced Ludwig Von Drake.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Paul Frees! [whispers] Welcome, foolish mortals. He's also the auctioneer in Pirates of the Caribbean.
